caption: United States v. Jackson
citation_line: United States v. Jackson, 862 F.3d 365 (3d Cir. 2017), with later sentencing appeals
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Hayden presided over the 2015 trial of John and Carolyn Jackson on federal and assimilated New Jersey child-endangerment charges arising from abuse of adopted children at Picatinny Arsenal, and imposed three successive sentencing judgments after appellate remands.
qualification_rationale: The prosecution attracted sustained press attention and produced repeated precedential guidance concerning the Assimilative Crimes Act, jury findings, causation and federal sentencing. It is career-significant despite—and partly because of—the unusual sequence of appellate reversals.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed the convictions but vacated Judge Hayden’s sentences three times. After the third remand it reassigned sentencing to Judge Wigenton, who imposed longer terms later affirmed in a precedential opinion.
